FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA MANAGEMENT’S REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended). Our internal control over financial reporting includes, among other things, defined policies and procedures for conducting and governing our business, sophisticated information systems for processing transactions, and a properly staffed, professional internal audit department. Mechanisms are in place to monitor the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting and actions are taken to correct all identified deficiencies. Our procedures for financial reporting include the active involvement of senior management, our Audit and Finance Committee, and our staff of highly qualified financial and legal professionals. Management, with the participation of our principal executive and financial officers, assessed our internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2026, the end of our fiscal year. Management based its assessment on criteria established in Internal Control — Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). Based on this assessment, management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of May 31, 2026. The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2026, has been audited by Ernst & Young LLP (PCAOB ID: 42 ), the independent registered public accounting firm who also audited the Company’s consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report. Ernst & Young LLP’s report on the Company’s internal control over financial reporting is included in this Annual Report. -66- Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm To the Stockholders and the Board of Directors of FedEx Corporation Opinion on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting We have audited FedEx Corporation’s internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2026, based on criteria established in Internal Control—Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). In our opinion, FedEx Corporation (the Company) maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2026, based on the COSO criteria. We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the consolidated balance sheets of the Company as of May 31, 2026 and 2025, the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in common stockholders’ investment for each of the three years in the period ended May 31, 2026, and the related notes and our report dated July 20, 2026 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon. Investments in equity securities with a readily determinable fair value are carried at fair value and are classified as Level 1 investments in the fair value hierarchy. Level 1 investments are valued at the closing price or last trade reported on the major market on which the individual securities are traded. For equity securities without readily determinable fair values that qualify for the net asset value (“NAV”) practical expedient, we have elected to apply the NAV practical -81- FEDEX CORPORATION NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS expedient to estimate fair value. Changes in fair value are included in “Other, net” in the accompanying consolidated statements of income. We apply the measurement alternative to all other investments in equity securities without a readily determinable fair value. Under the measurement alternative these equity securities are accounted for at cost, with adjustments for observable changes in prices and impairments included within “Other, net” in the accompanying consolidated statements of income. We perform a qualitative assessment each reporting period to evaluate whether these equity securities are impaired. Our assessment includes a review of recent operating results and trends and other publicly available data. If an investment is impaired, we write it down to its estimated fair value. Investments in debt securities, which are considered short-term investments, are classified as “available-for-sale” and are carried at fair value. Realized gains and losses on available-for-sale debt securities are included within “Other, net” in the accompanying consolidated statements of income while unrealized gains and losses, net of tax, are included within AOCL in the accompanying consolidated balance sheet. Investments in equity securities and debt securities are included within “Other assets” and “Prepaid expenses and other,” respectively, in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. On February 9, 2026, InPost S.A. (“InPost”) and a consortium including FedEx announced a conditional agreement on an intended recommended all-cash public offer for all issued and outstanding shares of InPost at an offer price of € 15.60 (cum dividend) per share (the “Offer”). Post-completion, the consortium will be structured with FedEx holding 37 %. InPost will continue to operate as a standalone company. The Offer and the transactions contemplated thereby (the “Transaction”) are subject to certain customary closing conditions, including, among others, the receipt of regulatory approvals. Based upon the proposed Offer price, FedEx’s investment is valued at approximately € 2.20 billion. FedEx intends to fund its portion of the Offer by utilizing available cash balances, existing or new liquidity sources, or a combination thereof. The Transaction is expected to be completed in the second half of calendar 2026. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION. credit_strengths.text: FedEx generates substantial operating cash flow that comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving meaningful free cash flow for debt service and shareholder returns. The annual trend shows operating cash flow rebounding strongly in the latest fiscal year after a prior-year dip, supporting the minimal indicative financial risk profile. This cash generation underpins the issuer's ability to fund its capital-intensive air courier network without straining liquidity.

The balance sheet carries a large unrestricted cash position that materially reduces net leverage relative to gross debt. Net debt to EBITDA sits well below the sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal. This provides a buffer against cyclical volume declines and supports the issuer's investment-grade-like credit characteristics, although the metric definition nets only cash and not short-term investments.

key_risks.text: FedEx's debt note discloses a significant maturity profile, with a large portion of long-term debt due after year five, but also meaningful near-term maturities. The issuer has demonstrated access to capital markets, refinancing maturing notes with new issuances. However, the weighted-average interest rate on long-term debt remains moderate, and any future refinancing at higher rates could pressure interest coverage, which already trails the sector median.

The risk-factor passage highlights FedEx's conditional agreement to acquire a minority stake in InPost, valued at approximately two point two billion euros, funded from available cash or new liquidity. This sizable outlay could absorb a portion of the issuer's cash buffer or increase leverage if debt-funded. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals, introducing execution and integration risk that may affect future cash flows and credit metrics.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage, measured by operating income over interest expense, is adequate but below the sector median, indicating less headroom than peers. The indicative financial risk profile remains minimal, but the coverage ratio has limited cushion against an earnings downturn. FedEx's substantial operating cash flow provides a secondary source of debt service, yet the relatively high gross debt load means interest costs are a meaningful fixed charge.

Free cash flow to debt is positive but modest, reflecting the capital-intensive nature of the air courier business. The ratio is below the sector median, suggesting that internally generated funds cover only a portion of debt obligations. However, the issuer's large cash balance and demonstrated market access mitigate refinancing risk. The debt maturity profile is well-laddered, with no single year presenting an unmanageable concentration.

overall_credit_view.text: FedEx presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, supported by strong operating cash flow, a substantial cash balance, and net leverage below the sector median. The issuer's scale and essential service positioning underpin revenue stability. However, operating margin and interest coverage trail sector medians, and the capital-intensive model requires ongoing investment. The InPost transaction introduces event risk, but funding flexibility and market access are adequate.

Analyst judgement: FedEx's credit trajectory is stable, with capacity to absorb moderate earnings volatility given threshold headroom. The debt maturity ladder is manageable, and the issuer has proactively refinanced maturities. However, shareholder distributions absorb a notable share of free cash flow, limiting deleveraging potential. A sustained decline in operating cash flow or a debt-funded acquisition could pressure the current minimal risk profile, warranting monitoring of leverage and coverage trends.

credit_strengths.text: FedEx產生龐大營運現金流，足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，並留下可觀的自由現金流用於償債及股東回報。年度趨勢顯示，營運現金流在上一財年下滑後，於最新財年強勁反彈，支撐最低的指示性財務風險狀況。此現金產生能力支持發行人在不對流動性構成壓力的情況下，為其資本密集型的航空快遞網絡提供資金。
資產負債表持有大量未受限現金，相對於總債務顯著降低淨槓桿。淨債務對EBITDA遠低於行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為最低。這為週期性貨量下滑提供緩衝，並支持發行人類投資級的信用特徵，儘管該指標定義僅扣除現金而不包括短期投資。

key_risks.text: FedEx的債務票據披露了重大的到期結構，大部分長期債務在五年後到期，但亦有可觀的近期到期債務。發行人已展示進入資本市場的能力，以新發行債券為到期票據再融資。然而，長期債務的加權平均利率仍屬溫和，未來若以更高利率再融資，可能對利息覆蓋率構成壓力，而該比率已落後於行業中位數。
風險因素章節強調，FedEx有條件同意收購InPost的少數股權，價值約為二十二億歐元，資金來自可用現金或新流動性。此巨額支出可能吸收發行人部分現金緩衝，或若以債務融資則增加槓桿。該交易仍有待監管批准，帶來執行及整合風險，可能影響未來現金流及信用指標。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率以營業收入除以利息支出衡量，屬充足但低於行業中位數，顯示較同業為少的緩衝空間。指示性財務風險狀況仍為最低，但覆蓋率對盈利下滑的緩衝有限。FedEx龐大的營運現金流提供次要的償債來源，然而相對較高的總債務負擔意味著利息成本是重大的固定支出。
自由現金流對債務比率為正但溫和，反映航空快遞業務的資本密集型性質。該比率低於行業中位數，顯示內部產生的資金僅覆蓋部分債務責任。然而，發行人龐大的現金餘額及已展示的市場準入能力緩解了再融資風險。債務到期結構分佈良好，沒有單一年份出現無法管理的集中度。

overall_credit_view.text: FedEx呈現最低的指示性財務風險狀況，受到強勁營運現金流、龐大現金餘額及低於行業中位數的淨槓桿所支持。發行人的規模及必要服務定位支撐收入穩定性。然而，營業利潤率及利息覆蓋率落後於行業中位數，且資本密集型模式需要持續投資。InPost交易帶來事件風險，但資金靈活性及市場準入能力充足。
分析師判斷：FedEx的信用軌跡穩定，考慮到閾值緩衝，具備吸收適度盈利波動的能力。債務到期階梯屬可管理，且發行人已主動為到期債務再融資。然而，股東分派佔據自由現金流的顯著份額，限制了去槓桿潛力。營運現金流持續下滑或債務融資收購可能對當前最低風險狀況構成壓力，值得監測槓桿及覆蓋率趨勢。
